The latest release brings the administration’s total commitment toward clearing inherited pension liabilities to N37bn, with the state government targeting full settlement of the backlog by April 2027.
This was disclosed in a statement issued by the Kano State Commissioner for Information and Home Affairs, Sanusi Bature, following the flag-off of the seventh tranche distribution at the Government House in Kano.
Speaking at the event, Yusuf described the non-payment of retirees’ entitlements after decades of service as an injustice, noting that his administration inherited a massive backlog accumulated over several years.
He assured pensioners still awaiting their entitlements that the government remains committed to clearing all outstanding liabilities through a transparent process before April 2027.
“The payments have continued to provide financial relief to thousands of households, ease economic hardship, and restore the dignity of retired public servants and families of deceased workers,” the governor stated, thanking retirees for their patience and sacrifices.
Yusuf commended the Kano State Pension Fund Trustees, the Office of the Head of Civil Service, the Ministry of Finance, and the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, led by its President, Godwin Abumisi, for facilitating the settlement programme.
He also appreciated the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, for his support for senior citizens’ welfare, while acknowledging recent recognitions from the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria and the Correspondents’ Association of Nigeria, which named him Friendly Governor of the Year 2026.
